evidence.claim: 3 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F on this transaction. Measured across the bank's closed cases, two or more failed flags is 2.9x more likely on confirmed fraud than on a cleared alarm (22.7% vs 7.9%)
13 transactions on this card in the 48 hours ending at the flagged one. A burst of ten or more is 1.9x more likely on confirmed fraud
The bank has 5 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-4957, CC-3682, CC-3327, CC-2935), pattern(s): account_takeover, out_of_region_use
The cardholder contacted the bank stating they did not make this purchase

Connected components place this card in the graph's giant device-sharing component (2,500 cards). Transitive device sharing percolates at every threshold tested, so membership is not evidence of a ring and carries no weight here; it is recorded because policy R6 asks for the shared element to be named.

Known fraud pattern 5: Account takeover: Account takeover. Mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number.

Policy rule R2: Customer denies the transaction: R2. Customer denies the transaction. Recommend `BLOCK_CARD` and `CREATE_CASE`. Add `FILE_REPORT` if exposure exceeds $1,000 or the case connects to a shared device profile or another card's fraud.

case.summary: On 2016-12-10, the cardholder reported that they did not make a $49.00 in person transaction on card C08623-K2. Against the transaction, 3 of the card-detail match flags M1-M9 came back F, and 13 transactions occurred on this card in the 48 hours ending at the flagged one. The card is linked to 5 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on it (CC-4957, CC-3682, CC-3327, CC-2935), and the case was assessed as account_takeover at probability 0.95 with exposure of $49.00.
